title: Feeding instead
hook: those who can never fast feed a poor person each day

segments.voice: Yesterday, qada': made up later. Missed fasts aren't erased, only moved, and Aisha paid hers back in Sha'ban.

A grandmother sits at the iftar table every evening of Ramadan. She hasn't fasted in years. Her body can't do it anymore, and her doctor has said so plainly. Yesterday's answer, make the days up later, doesn't help her: there is no later when she'll be stronger. So is she outside the fast now, watching from the edge of the table? The verse that gave the sick and the traveler their other days has one more line. It gives her a way to take part.
screen: `A GRANDMOTHER AT THE IFTAR TABLE.` → `NO LATER WHEN SHE'LL BE STRONGER.` → `ONE MORE LINE IN THE VERSE.`

segments.voice: The word is fidyah. First, the verse. Surah two, verse one hundred eighty-four, after the sick and the traveler, says in Pickthall's words that there is "a ransom: the feeding of a man in need." Fidyah is something given in place of something else: here, a meal for a person in need, in place of a day of fasting. Second, who it's for. Readers have argued over this verse, because it can sound as though anyone may feed instead of fasting. A report in Sahih al-Bukhari gives the reading of Ibn Abbas, the Prophet's cousin: the verse is for the old man and the old woman who cannot fast; they feed a poor person for each day. Scholars extend that to people with a lasting illness and no hope of recovery. So fidyah is for those for whom qada' will never be possible. Third, how it's done. The schools differ on the measure, a portion of grain or its value, or a meal, and on whether it's paid day by day or all at once. Some mosques and charities publish a figure each Ramadan, and some families pay it on behalf of a parent. The same verse adds that whoever does more good of their own accord, it is better for them. Fourth, why this matters. The fast isn't only about the person who's hungry; it turns toward the one who is hungry every day. When a body can no longer fast, the fast doesn't disappear. It becomes a plate set in front of someone else.
screen: `FIDYAH: GIVEN IN PLACE OF.` · `FOR THOSE WHO CAN NEVER FAST.` · `ONE PERSON FED FOR EACH DAY.` · `THE FAST BECOMES A PLATE.` · then, large: `A RANSOM: THE FEEDING OF A MAN IN NEED.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who can no longer do something they once loved, an older relative, a friend who's ill, a neighbor who doesn't leave the house. Then plan one meal, or the cost of one, to give to someone hungry, quietly, with that person in your heart. If they owe fidyah, you might offer to help them pay it, and if you pray, remember them in it.
Fidyah. Feeding a person in need for each day of Ramadan, given by those who can never fast or make the days up. Today's word.
Your line: feed instead. When you can't give what was asked, you give what you still can. Same time tomorrow.
